title: Ἔχις καὶ ἀλώπηξ
part: The Viper and the Fox (Chambry 115 · Perry 96)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 115 (= Perry 96). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἔχις ἐπὶ παλιούρων δέσμῃ ὑπὲρ ποταμὸν παρεφέρετο.
sentences.tr: Echis epi paliourōn desmēi hyper potamon parephereto.
sentences.l: A viper was being carried along on a bundle of thorn-branches over a river.
sentences.n: παλίουρος is Christ's thorn, a scrubby thorn-bush; a cut bundle of it makes a raft only in the sense that it floats. παραφέρομαι is to be carried past, swept along — the viper is not steering.

sentences.t: Ἀλώπηξ δὲ παριοῦσα, ὡς ἐθεάσατο αὐτόν, εἶπεν· « Ἄξιος τῆς νηὸς ὁ ναύκληρος. »
sentences.tr: Alōpēx de pariousa, hōs etheasato auton, eipen· « Axios tēs nēos ho nauklēros. »
sentences.l: And a fox passing by, when she caught sight of him, said: « Worthy of the ship is the skipper. »
sentences.i: A fox passing by caught sight of him and said: « The skipper is a match for the ship. »
sentences.n: ἄξιος with the genitive is 'worth as much as, on a par with' — the fox is not paying a compliment: a vile cargo on a vile vessel, each deserving the other. νηός is the Ionic and poetic genitive of ναῦς; the Attic form νεώς stands in the fable just before this one. ναύκληρος is properly the shipowner who sails his own vessel.

sentences.t: Πρὸς ἄνδρα πονηρὸν μοχθηροῖς πράγμασιν ἐγχειρήσαντα.
sentences.tr: Pros andra ponēron mochthērois pragmasin encheirēsanta.
sentences.l: Against a wicked man who has set his hand to villainous business.
sentences.n: The moral is a bare heading with no verb at all — Chambry's page gives only the target, 'against such-and-such a man', and the reader supplies the rest. ἐγχειρέω, 'to put a hand to', takes the dative of the thing undertaken.
